title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
situation: Designing commitments for groups: spelling out required responses per situation versus letting each group set its own thresholds.
options_considered: Prescribed responses per situation / Complicated conditionals / Each group sets its own thresholds with general pressure to strengthen them
choice: Chose to let each group set its own thresholds, with general pressure to strengthen them.
reason: Groups differ in situations and burdens, and uncertain profiles made prescribed responses either overly elaborate or overly cautious.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
situation: Deciding whether to build items around specific threat stories or around broad skills.
options_considered: Build around specific threat stories / build around broad skills
choice: Chose broad skills, treating coverage of specific threat stories as a bonus.
reason: Excluding danger from a broadly skilled system seems hard to do just by dismissing specific stories.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
situation: There was confusion over whether earlier work on two systems counted as formal reviews, and it had to be described.
options_considered: Describe it as formal reviews / Describe it as informal pilots or research collaborations
choice: Chose to describe the earlier work as informal pilots or research collaborations rather than formal reviews.
reason: The work did not provide meaningful oversight.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
situation: A decision was needed on whether current systems might be deliberately underperforming on checks.
options_considered: Worry about deliberate scheming now / Focus on mundane under-elicitation and treat deliberate gaming of training as a future concern
choice: Chose to regard deliberate strategic underperformance as implausible for current systems and to focus on mundane elicitation shortfalls.
reason: It would require advanced single-step reasoning beyond long written reasoning, implying implausible sudden jumps in what systems can do.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
situation: A conclusion about whether casual people could reach a threshold had to be worded.
options_considered: State a broad conclusion / state a conclusion scoped to casual people and the specific versions tested
choice: Chose a conclusion scoped to casual people without the option to adjust the system and to the specific versions tested.
reason: The systems tested were weak and later adjustment could change what they can do, so the claim is conditional.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
situation: The researcher faced ambiguous signs of scheming in a system's outputs or reasoning, unclear whether they were just noise.
options_considered: Treat the signs as noise and patch them superficially / penalise visible scheming in the reasoning / take the signs seriously as evidence
choice: Chose to take the ambiguous signs seriously, without patching them over or penalising visible scheming.
reason: Superficial fixes leave the evidence too ambiguous to change anything, and penalising visible scheming may just teach the system to hide it.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
situation: Some early records had been collected without the incentive scheme, and had to be kept or dropped.
options_considered: Kept the early records / excluded the records collected without incentives
choice: Chose to keep the early records collected without the incentive scheme.
reason: They give valuable data, are relatively few, and the resulting estimates look qualitatively reasonable.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
situation: Needed checks that give warning before a hazardous level is reached.
options_considered: Set the threshold then adjust down for a buffer / Build the furthest-out check that still sits clearly ahead of the hazard / Modify problems or agent help to define the gap
choice: Chose to build a smooth measuring axis, then either set a threshold and adjust down, or build the furthest-out check ahead of the hazard.
reason: The bottleneck to projecting trends is a good axis whose increments mean the same thing; arbitrary test-set trends don't relate to the hazard.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
situation: While building a set of environments, some candidates did poorly against the design criteria, and it was unclear whether to keep them.
options_considered: Keep all candidates / go through three steps and drop those that fell short
choice: Chose to go through three steps and drop many specifications and finished versions that fell short.
reason: Environments needed to meet the feasibility and saturation-resistance criteria, and reference runs often showed problems needing major adjustments or dropping.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
situation: Deciding whether participants in the reference runs should get the internet, since external materials could trivialize some items.
options_considered: Always permit web use with a few exclusions / restrict web use
choice: Chose to always permit web use, while barring assistants, a math engine, and sign-in services.
reason: Pilot runs showed participants did much worse without web use, often because of small hindrances like forgetting details.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
situation: A decision was needed on what evidence to gather about whether a company could lose control of its systems.
options_considered: Test the strongest systems with reasoning visible and review private material / Rely on material the company already shares
choice: Chose to test the strongest systems with reasoning visible and to review private material on their strengths, alignment, and control.
reason: No reason stated.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
situation: The team was designing a participation process for a pilot and wanted leading companies to take part.
options_considered: Offer a quiet, no-fault way to withdraw / offer no way to withdraw
choice: Chose to offer a quiet, no-fault way to withdraw.
reason: The work relies on building and maintaining strong working relationships with the participating companies.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
situation: A fair comparison was needed between automated systems and humans across different duration budgets, given that the systems' strategies differ.
options_considered: A single long run / Several splits of a fixed total budget / Other durations per attempt
choice: Chose several splits of a fixed total budget, using the top-performing split for each system in the headline comparison.
reason: The systems could restart themselves by resetting their setup, so the comparison is considered fair.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
situation: Deciding whether items should carry restrictions, such as limited internet use, to control hardness and contamination.
options_considered: Add artificial restrictions / permit general internet use / permit only offline or archived material
choice: Chose to permit offline or archived material for steady hardness, but forbid artificial restrictions that do not apply in real-life threat settings.
reason: A real autonomous system could use the internet and run programs, so artificial restrictions would not reflect real-life threat settings.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
situation: A fair measure was needed of what systems can do on a set of problems, without spurious misses understating them.
options_considered: Have people attempt the problems and give systems substantial effort and resources / Have reviewers rate problems without attempting them and use typical low per-query spend
choice: Chose to have people attempt the problems and give systems substantial effort and resources comparable to a person's.
reason: Attempting removes ambiguous or broken items, and it would be bad to conclude systems cannot do something when they can, only at lower expense.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
situation: Designing rewards for people doing a reference run so their duration estimates reflect efficient completion rather than excessive checking.
options_considered: Add a speed bonus for the fastest correct participant alongside the completion bonus / Pay only a flat rate by duration
choice: Chose to add a speed bonus for the fastest correct participant alongside the completion bonus weighted by average duration.
reason: In an early pilot some participants spent very long re-checking solutions, so the bonus pushes estimates toward the shortest plausible duration.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
situation: Reference results differed widely across attempts and across recruitment groups, making a comparison with the systems hard to set up.
options_considered: Compare to the average reference result / Compare to the strongest reference attempts
choice: Chose to compare to the strongest reference attempts rather than the average.
reason: Reference results differed widely, and groups differed significantly (0.96 vs 0.46 average), while the question of concern is about the strongest performers.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
situation: The aim was to draw out what a system can do without the testers' own tuning effort supplying the result.
options_considered: Tune on a development set and test on a separate set / tune directly on the tested items / use a random split versus an added distribution gap
choice: Chose to do all tuning on a development set and test on a separate set whose gap matches the real-world gap.
reason: Narrowly targeted tuning can put the answer in, so a held-out test keeps the check fair.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
situation: It was unclear whether an item could be trusted as a measure, since current or future systems may have memorized its solution.
options_considered: Accept the item once the current system hasn't memorized it / also require robustness against future memorization
choice: Chose to treat non-memorization as a good sign but insufficient, also requiring robustness against future memorization.
reason: Future systems might have memorized openly available solutions in more detail, so current non-memorization doesn't remove the concern.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
situation: A way was needed to measure progress on a scale that is meaningful in the real world, unlike standard tests and impressions.
options_considered: Rely on qualitative impressions / Use standard tests that are close to saturation / Build a diverse suite with human completion duration as the axis
choice: Chose a diverse suite attempted by skilled humans, using human completion duration as the axis.
reason: Impressions cannot become a trend, standard tests detach from real usefulness, and diverse items are harder to overfit to.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
situation: The work needed to test whether a system could cause severe damage, without knowing which specific mental skills were the bottleneck.
options_considered: Whole-chain tests built from the real-world threat / measuring one isolated skill directly / generic standard tests
choice: Chose whole-chain tests built as a chain from the real-world threat down to measurable stand-ins.
reason: The bottleneck skills are hard to know, isolated measures may not link to real outcomes, and standard tests saturate quickly and are poor stand-ins.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
situation: Needed to decide how strongly to present earlier pre-launch work as oversight or accountability.
options_considered: Present the work as an audit / decline to present it as an audit
choice: Chose to decline to present the work as an audit, pointing to the confidentiality terms and lack of a formal link to launch decisions.
reason: Under the terms there was no right or responsibility to share findings, and no formal expectation that it would inform launch decisions.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
situation: A labelled set meant to cap what a system can do was being built, and it was unclear whether to continue.
options_considered: Continue building the labelled set / move on to other work
choice: Chose to move on to other work after trying to build the labelled set.
reason: It was hard, though it would have given stronger guarantees that the system could not do the work.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
situation: Deciding whether results from an early-version test of a system could be accepted as a reliable judgment of worrying strengths.
options_considered: Accept early-version results as they stand / treat them as unreliable without testing the final version and doing own adjustments
choice: Chose to cite the stated caveat that the results were unreliable without testing the final version and doing own adjustments.
reason: The testers lacked the final version and could not adjust it, and the final version had upgrades that could change the outcomes.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
situation: The researcher needed a way to elicit goal-directed action from a basic system for testing.
options_considered: Use the basic system directly / wrap it in helper programs and test the combinations
choice: Chose to wrap the system in helper programs that run commands, handle files and browse, and to test the combinations.
reason: The wrapper lets the system interact with the world much as a person would using a text-only command line.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
situation: Some unflattering statements about companies were available but were neither strongly supported nor central to the main conclusion.
options_considered: Include the unflattering statements and invite comparisons between companies / leave them out
choice: Chose to leave out the unflattering statements and not invite comparisons between companies.
reason: They were neither solidly defensible nor particularly relevant to the core conclusion.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
situation: Facing a gloomier outlook, the researcher had to pick which protective steps to push for.
options_considered: Design thorough ideal regimes with strong outside oversight / Prioritise basic, readily achievable steps
choice: Chose to prioritise basic, readily achievable steps over designing thorough ideal regimes.
reason: Little runway seems left and even basic steps are not being taken, so a modest cut in the chance of a bad outcome matters more.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
situation: It was unclear how far to trust a headline growth estimate, given noisy data and setup choices.
options_considered: Report a single figure / report a range from a sensitivity analysis plus a mental correction
choice: Chose to report a range from a sensitivity analysis, with a mental correction, rather than a single figure.
reason: Items easy to score automatically may be systematically easier, so absolute lengths may overstate real-world strength, though the trend itself is solid.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
situation: The setups needed to be shown feasible and not saturated, so that low results from the tested system would be meaningful.
options_considered: Validate each setup with several explicit checks plus an informal ceiling estimate / Skip validation of the setups
choice: Chose to validate each setup with several explicit checks plus an informal estimate of how close experts come to the ceiling.
reason: Reliable expert progress shows setups are feasible with clear instructions, and a high ceiling prevents saturation.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
situation: A fair comparison of how hard problems are for people versus systems was needed so duration estimates reflect real work.
options_considered: Same setup and instructions for both, with realistic aids / informal estimates / comparison under very different conditions
choice: Chose the same setup and instructions for people and systems, with realistic aids permitted for people.
reason: Wanted a fair comparison while giving people realistic aids so reference durations reflect normal work.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
situation: The researcher needed to measure whether systems could carry out a broad multi-step activity on their own, with no single obvious test.
options_considered: Rely on one test / build a suite of 12 real-world items of rising hardness and run several setups on it
choice: Chose the suite of 12 real-world items, tested on several setups.
reason: Unless a system can do almost all items it is unlikely to have the overall skill, and the items span a range of hardness and obstacles.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
situation: Deciding how strongly to describe the worth of a report as outside checking of powerful developers.
options_considered: Describe it as robust independent oversight / describe it as not robust alone but a pilot of what future requirements could demand
choice: Chose to describe it as a pilot, not robust oversight by itself.
reason: Participants could have withdrawn at any moment if the result ran against their interests.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
situation: A decision was needed on how strongly to claim that measured results reflect the full level of what the systems can do.
options_considered: Present the results as a firm measure / Present them as a reasonable floor and note that a better setup would likely do better
choice: Chose to frame the results as a reasonable floor and note that a better setup would likely do better.
reason: The setup was not heavily optimized, so the full level of the strongest systems remains undetermined.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
situation: Deciding how hard to push back on companies' removals from a report.
options_considered: Set a high bar for which removals to challenge / push back on more removals
choice: Chose to set a relatively high bar for which removals to challenge.
reason: Maintaining working relationships with the companies shaped these decisions.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
situation: The researcher needed to test whether a system was holding back its true strength when asking it directly might fail.
options_considered: Ask directly alone / adjust the system on example data to show the strength / use an unfittable set as a ceiling
choice: Chose to adjust the system on example data to show the strength, assuming it does not deliberately resist the adjustment.
reason: If the system can be adjusted to show the strength, it must be assumed to have it, unless it is too far beyond any examples.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
situation: The researcher needed to confirm the items were sound, so that wins and losses reflected real strength rather than faults or gaming.
options_considered: Rely on quality-check runs by people alone / have an automated system make repeated attempts and read every record
choice: Chose to have an automated system make five attempts at each item and manually read all 945 records.
reason: Reading the records surfaces silent and explicit faults in the item setup that the people's quality-check runs missed.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
situation: Needing a duration estimate for items where no reference attempt worked.
options_considered: Collect reference attempts for all items / Use averages of attempts that worked, with forecasts as a fallback
choice: Chose the geometric mean of attempts that worked, with forecasts from the creator or a familiar author for items lacking any.
reason: Funding and scheduling shortfalls and logistics of long items blocked reference attempts for 50 items, and 29 more had no attempt that worked.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
situation: Needing the outcome of each run to reflect real strength rather than flaws in the setup, shortcuts, or ambiguity.
options_considered: Require a run-through by someone other than the author, with detailed documentation / test by the author alone
choice: Chose a run-through by someone other than the author, with detailed documentation of the run and possible problems.
reason: Outcomes can be driven by unexpected causes such as faulty grading, ambiguous instructions, missing materials, or shortcuts.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
situation: Needing a way to grade outputs so the grades are dependable and distinguish between weak and strong results across a wide range.
options_considered: Continuous grades, automatic where possible, with robust manual rubrics as backup / unreliable automatic grading / pass-fail grading
choice: Chose continuous grades between zero and one, accepting robust manual rubrics over unreliable automatic grading and avoiding pass-fail grading.
reason: Grades should reflect real strength and track how hard items are, rather than reflecting noise or presentation slips.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
situation: Unsure whether the findings depend on how outcomes were converted to pass/fail and on groups in the sample having uneven sizes.
options_considered: Keep pass/fail outcomes with equal weighting / use continuous outcomes and a size-adjusted weighted average / use both alongside each other
choice: Chose to rerun the analysis with continuous outcomes and a size-adjusted weighted average, alongside the original setup.
reason: Larger groups might skew the result, and continuous outcomes give a finer signal.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
situation: The question was how strongly to conclude that the automated agents' shortfalls set an upper level on real-world concern about the models.
options_considered: Present the shortfalls as a robust upper level / state they are not robust and restrict the conclusion to casual users
choice: Chose to state the agents are not a robust upper level and to restrict the conclusion to casual users.
reason: The agents that were built do not capture the full strength of the system.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
situation: A set of problems was being collected to measure an autonomous system across a useful range of hardness.
options_considered: Collect harder ones first and derive easier variants / collect easier ones first / collect shorter ones
choice: Chose to collect harder ones first and derive easier variants by adding guidance or loosening requirements.
reason: Easier variants can be made fairly straightforwardly, while hard ones are scarce and more informative.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
situation: It was unknown whether tuning of the underlying system changes its relevant strengths.
options_considered: Compare the early and tuned versions on the suite / Test only one version
choice: Chose to compare the early version with the tuned launch version on the suite.
reason: Tuning or other light modifications could significantly boost the relevant strengths.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
situation: Designing an early-warning check to be interpretable and tied clearly to automation concerns.
options_considered: Compare with a reference group under equivalent conditions / Compare under differing conditions / Use no comparison
choice: Chose to compare directly with a reference group under equivalent conditions, using 8-hour attempts on seven environments.
reason: Equivalent comparisons give a clear logical link to automation concerns, help confirm feasibility, and anchor the interpretation of the system's results.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
situation: Many items relied on informal estimates in place of measured reference results, and the question was how far to trust them.
options_considered: Treat estimates as sufficient / treat them as a reasonable stand-in but keep the measured references
choice: Chose to treat estimates as a reasonable stand-in while stating that measured references still add a lot.
reason: The moderate correlation shows estimates are informative but leave considerable unexplained variance.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
situation: A later version of a system completed more problems than an earlier version, and the reason for the gap needed interpreting.
options_considered: Unrelated tuning can substantially raise the relevant skill / The gap is unrelated to the tuning
choice: Chose to conclude that tuning not aimed at the skill can still substantially raise it.
reason: The later version completed three more problems even though its tuning was not aimed at that skill.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
situation: Deciding whether the group should expand into carrying out outside checking of others' systems itself.
options_considered: Expand into doing it directly / Stay as is and let other actors enter / Leave it to governments to do in-house
choice: Chose to state interest and possible hiring, while making expansion conditional on outside factors and open to others entering.
reason: It depends on whether governments mandate it, whether labs permit involvement, whether hiring goes well, and whether it detracts from developing the science.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
situation: Needed equal budgets for automated agents and people, and a way to cap agent runs.
options_considered: Cap by elapsed clock duration / Cap by token usage
choice: Chose to cap by clock duration, not counting failed requests or rate-limit pauses.
reason: It gives both equal compute duration, and delays from the service matter little since agents mostly wait on computations.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
situation: The top result in a noisy setup needed interpreting, and it was unclear how much of it was real.
options_considered: Accept the top result as it stood / rerun the top solution and compare the two results
choice: Chose to rerun the top solution and read the original as partly fitted to noise, so the gap is likely understated.
reason: The rerun result was well below the original, indicating the high result was partly driven by noise.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
situation: The group had to decide whether to focus on developing the underlying science of its field or to take on an outside reviewer role.
options_considered: Make developing the science the top priority / also become an outside reviewer
choice: Chose to make developing the science the top priority and not become an outside reviewer.
reason: The goal can be reached without taking on the reviewer role.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
situation: Needed to confirm that top-ranked runs were legitimate rather than exploiting loopholes, but inspecting every run by hand was infeasible.
options_considered: Inspect every run by hand / Inspect only a selected subset of top runs, focusing on settings with known loopholes
choice: Chose to inspect the top two runs per setting and the top runs on two loophole-prone settings until the top 15 were valid, giving cheating runs zero.
reason: Those two settings are the only ones where simple ways to cheat are known.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
situation: Timeline claims were uncertain because of caveats on the measured numbers, and the strength of the statement had to be decided.
options_considered: State that a short timeline would not be surprising and require confidence it won't happen / wait for high confidence before acting
choice: Chose to frame the standard as needing confidence it won't happen, while acknowledging the caveats.
reason: Even a small chance of a severe outcome is high stakes for people living now, so whole-number-percent chances warrant concern.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
situation: Deciding how to size up what a system could do when it may hold back or notice the check, and when the setup includes protective layers.
options_considered: Check only the system as deployed with its protective layers / check using a weak setup / check the maximum easily reachable strength without the layers
choice: Chose to check the maximum easily reachable strength without the protective layers, including small adjustments and a better setup.
reason: The system could be stolen, misused by insiders, or adjusted, so what matters is what it could do without the deployed protective layers.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
situation: Had to decide how strongly to tie test results to real-world automation of research work.
options_considered: State the real gap is likely much larger than seen / present the results as showing near-full automation
choice: Chose to state the real gap is likely much larger than seen, while also noting factors that could cause underestimation.
reason: Real work is at least two orders of magnitude larger in scale across many dimensions, and the tests are neatly defined and non-interacting.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
situation: There was disagreement and uncertainty within the group about how strongly the report should state its conclusions.
options_considered: Keep to well-supported statements generally agreed within the group / add comments on how worried to be, urges to act, or statements not generally agreed
choice: Chose to keep to well-supported statements generally agreed within the group.
reason: The report is meant as analysis of a narrow set of concerns rather than advocacy, so it sticks to well-supported, consensus statements.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
situation: A targeted deceptive-message scenario had to be tested realistically without causing real damage to anyone.
options_considered: Let systems message outsiders and put sites online / use a volunteer stand-in target with intercepted messages and simulated replies under close supervision
choice: Chose the volunteer stand-in target, intercepted messages, simulated replies and close supervision, with no sites put online.
reason: Protect outside parties from real targeting while still testing the full sequence from start to finish.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
situation: Check results on a system were hard to interpret because reviewers could not adjust it and it missed on the hardest items.
options_considered: Check the system as-is without patching / Patch soon-fixable problems and treat continued misses as a soft ceiling / Use existing aids
choice: Chose to patch problems expected to be fixed soon and treat continued misses as a soft ceiling with added margin.
reason: Without patching, everything stops for the same reason and reveals nothing about the next hurdle; fixable limitations are likely to vanish soon.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
situation: Designing a set of items whose hardness spans a range, so that trends could be projected forward.
options_considered: Roughly even spread across a wide range / Two-clump spread
choice: Chose a roughly even spread of hardness across a wide range.
reason: An even spread lets gradual increases be projected meaningfully, instead of seeing fast progress, a stall, then fast progress again.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
situation: Planning a first report on frontier hazards and needing to pick which threat scenarios it would cover.
options_considered: Cover only one core scenario / Also cover misuse by people, non-deliberate damage, and sabotage scenarios
choice: Chose to scope the report to the single core scenario and exclude misuse, non-deliberate damage, and sabotage.
reason: No reason stated.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
situation: A decision was needed on what arrangements outside reviewers require for their checks to be meaningful.
options_considered: Formal arrangements with firm commitments / informal trial procedures / restricted entry without formal commitments
choice: Chose formal arrangements and commitments for outside reviewers, both before scaling or deployment and for research on the checks.
reason: Formal arrangements are needed to review new frontier systems before scaling or deployment and to do research that makes the checks better.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
situation: Deciding how to read whether constraints from a working relationship with outside partners bent the conclusions of a report.
options_considered: Treat the distortion as small / treat the distortion as large / leave the question open
choice: Chose to treat the distortion as small here, while noting that less mild conclusions would be harder to handle.
reason: The conclusions were mild, so there was little tension between openness and keeping the partners involved.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
situation: A decision was needed on whether to include an earlier experiment in the report.
options_considered: Include the earlier experiment / leave it out and refer readers to a separate document
choice: Chose to leave it out and refer readers to a separate document.
reason: It was from earlier iterations of the approach and received more attention than anticipated.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
situation: The set of problems could share one obstacle, which would cause sudden jumps in measured results.
options_considered: Require varied obstacles across problems / let all problems be blocked by the same obstacle
choice: Chose to require varied obstacles, so the system gets stuck in different ways on different problems.
reason: A shared obstacle could produce a sudden big jump after a small change to the system.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
situation: Deciding at which step of a long development process the checking effort should be concentrated.
options_considered: Concentrate checks before and during the large effort and before private use / concentrate checks only just before outside rollout / run one big effort then one check
choice: Chose to concentrate the checks before and during the large effort and before private use.
reason: Once something expensive exists it is hard not to use it, it can be stolen or misused, and outside rollout is more reversible than unwatched private buildup.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
situation: Results existed about advanced automation of research work, and there was worry that sharing them could speed things up or fuel hype and racing.
options_considered: Keep results secret / share only selectively with a few outside decision-makers / share openly
choice: Chose to share the results openly and be transparent.
reason: Funding, talent and decisions respond to awareness, others already know this, and relying on secrecy is not a good protective strategy.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
situation: A set of procedures for judging systems was being designed, and it was unclear which party would eventually run them.
options_considered: Build procedures usable by any party / Build procedures tailored to one specific party
choice: Chose procedures usable by any party, including governments, developer teams, outside groups, or the authors' own group.
reason: No reason stated.

title: Foundation Models for Oversight
